title: Dynamic quantization-aware kernel tiling and attention split for long-context prefill
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: For long-context workloads (> 4k tokens) we observe that prefill time is dominated by attention kernel runtime and dequant/repquant overhead when using INT8/FP8 execution paths. Current kernels either (a) use a single monolithic attention implementation which forces large GEMM shapes and high peak memory, or (b) apply a static tiling that doesn't match the runtime sequence length and KV-cache alignment, causing extra copies and dequantization steps.

Goal: Implement a dynamic, quantization-aware kernel selection strategy that: (1) splits attention work into windowed-local + global components where applicable, (2) picks per-request tiling and kernel variant optimized for the observed sequence-length distribution and hardware, and (3) minimizes dequant/convert overhead by aligning tile boundaries with packed INT8 representations and KV cache layout. This should reduce prefill latency and overall token cost while preserving model quality (no >1% perplexity regression on eval suites).

High-level approach:
1) Profiling pass: collect sequence-length distribution and hardware microbenchmarks for candidate attention tiles (tile sizes: 64, 128, 256, 512) on target GPUs. Store per-model/per-instance tile performance and numeric stability metadata in the kernel registry.
2) Attention split: implement a kernel-level split that separates local windowed attention (dense, small tiles) from sparse/global attention (smaller full-attention kernel). For models with rotary/ALiBi or sparse patterns, the router will prefer windowed kernels to reduce compute.
3) Quantization-aware tiling: kernels will operate directly on packed INT8 blocks where possible; when accumulation requires higher precision, use FP16/FP32 accumulators but avoid full dequantize-to-FP32 for entire KV rows. Introduce a lightweight re-quantization epilogue that only touches tiles that cross cache boundaries.
4) Runtime decision: implement a runtime selector that, per-request, picks the kernel variant (INT8-windowed, INT8-global, mixed-precision, or FP16 fallback) using a cost model that includes latency, numeric risk score, and cache alignment penalties. Emit telemetry events capturing selected variant and observed timings for continuous improvement.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs benefit: Additional kernel variants and registry metadata increase maintenance burden but allow large wins for long-context workloads.
- Numeric stability: Aggressive INT8 for Q/K improves perf but can regress logits in tail cases; we mitigate with model-specific risk scores and automatic fallback thresholds.
- Memory vs copies: Tiling reduces peak memory but can introduce boundary copies; we favor tile alignments that match existing KV packed layout to avoid copies where possible.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prefill latency reduced by >= 12% for 8k token synthetic workload on p4d-like instance compared to current INT8 baseline while maintaining throughput within 5% of baseline.
No more than 1% relative increase in perplexity on standard evaluation prompts for candidate models when using chosen INT8/FP8 kernels vs FP16 reference.
Kernel registry contains per-model tile-performance entries and numeric-stability flags for the primary family of models (gpt-like and longform variants).
Telemetry emits selection events for each request and a nightly aggregation shows selection distribution and any fallbacks triggered.
Unit and integration tests for tile alignment correctness, KV-cache pointer arithmetic, and re-quant epilogue edge cases are in CI and passing.
Rollout plan with canary traffic and automatic rollback on >10% latency/quality regression configured in console rollouts.
implementation_notes: Add profiling harness that runs candidate tile sizes across a matrix of seq_len, batch_size, and kv-cache occupancy; store results in kernel registry (JSON).
Implement two new attention kernels: windowed_int8_attn and global_int8_attn. Each exposes tile-size parameter and alignment precondition API so runtime can verify suitability before selection.
Create lightweight re-quant epilogue: reads INT8 accumulator tiles, applies FP16 accumulation -> per-tile scaling -> write packed INT8 to KV cache, avoiding full tensor dequantize.
Extend kernel registry API to include numeric-risk-score and fallback_threshold. Provide tooling to update risk scores from offline stability sweeps.
Integrate runtime selector into request path: sampling-based initial selection (first N requests use validated safe kernel), then switch to cost-model driven selection for steady-state.
Ensure KV cache layout supports tile-aligned appends: if request's prefill would misalign, perform a single boundary coalesce operation rather than per-tile copies.
Add CI microbench tests that assert tile kernels are within 5% of profiled numbers to detect regressions early.
Document numeric safety caveats and how to force FP16 via model pin or per-customer policy in Redwood Console.
benchmarks: Target: 12%+ latency reduction on prefill stage vs current int8-monolithic baseline measured on p4d-variant. Record p50/p95/p99 and end-to-end prefill time.
Quality target: perplexity change <= 1% measured on eval set rwd-long-eval-v2 when using selected INT8 path.
Resource target: peak GPU memory usage not to exceed FP16 baseline by more than 5% for same workload when using mixed precision kernels.
risks: Numeric regressions in corner cases for very long contexts or adversarial prompts; mitigated via nightly eval sweeps and automatic fallback thresholds.
Maintenance overhead from multiple kernel variants; mitigate with comprehensive test coverage and clear deprecation policy.
Unanticipated hardware-specific performance drop (some GPUs may favor larger tiles); include hardware-specific profiles and conservative defaults.
Telemetry noise if selector misreports due to async timings; include instrumentation validation and TTL-based deduplication.
